reviews.comment: Do not take this class.

Dr Yadav was great! She made it clear what she was looking for and it was shown through the quizzes. The course does 1 week notes and a quiz, then the next week would be a discussion and an assignment. Pretty easy, just stay on top of your work. I recommend this as a fun science credit!

Out of all 6 of my classes, this class had the most busy work. There is minimum 5 assignments every week. The instructions are never clear and you have to HUNT for them. The communication is very poor and she is not very accessible over email. Biweekly zooms with three different groups of 5-6 people. There are better courses that would be worth it

This class is 90% group work and projects which is very hard for an online course. She was the most unorganized prof ever. You were always searching to find instructions. She is virtually absent in the class and you're grading peer essays along with the TAs. Do NOT take this for a CD course. It was so much more work than it is worth.

Do not take this class if you do not want to sign up for a scavenger hunt to figure out how to do assignments. Instructions are unclear 9 times out of 10, you will never know where to turn stuff in or what is expected of you, and the professor does not even answer any questions. There are easier online CDs out there or take a different prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of assignments and discussion post but its pretty easy to get an A if you just keep up with due dates and do the bare minimum.

This class was really easy, but I didn't learn anything. She isn't super friendly over email. If you complete the assignments on time you will end with an A. The level of work you submit doesn't really matter.

The most unorganized class ever. I took this class online, and it was the worst class with so much work. There are biweekly zooms that you have to schedule with random people that are the biggest pain to deal with. Also, these people change after every 3 units. Avoid this class there are much better cultural discourse classes you can take.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is easy, so if you need a GPA booster and can't find any other class to take, I'd recommend this. But she is unable to communicate effectively, and she doesn't grade your essays, which are worth most of your grade. She instead uses Peerceptiv, which has your peers grade your essays. Overall, time-consuming and annoying to deal with.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a great professor and can communicate really well, except that it is very time-consuming. This is the only class that requires more work than any other class I've had this semester. I'd advise you not to take this class if you have a heavy major that requires lots of studying. But if you do, be prepared to make time.
Class is based on discussions and peer graded essays. Not incredibly time consuming. Overall, an easy class, can knock out most assignments for the week pretty quickly.

Geog 205 was a great online course. The course consists of essays graded by other students on Peerceptiv, group discussions on Zoom, and several online quizzes. I would recommend taking this class as it is very flexible, manageable, and Professor Yadav offers multiple opportunities for extra credit. An A is highly attainable! Recommend.
The exams were not very difficult, but the labs were confusing and time consuming. Feedback on labs and the group project was helpful.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class wasnt difficult but very annoying with the many deadlines each week. Used Peerceptiv and if you forget to peer grade someones work or review THEIR COMMENTS on your paper? Bam 75 on essay The essay process releases in waves on specific days instead of it all being handed out in the beginning. Does give lots of extra credit tho

6 total essays (500-700 words) & easy biweekly quizzes. Id write all of the essays the day of and still get As. Uses Peerceptiv if that's a turn off, but it's so minor that I'd get 30% accuracy with peers and keep an A. Only annoying thing was scheduling meetings, after it's basically a free 100 for participating. Tons of extra credit 30+ points.

I personally believe that he was not a bad professor as it is an online class. What I can agree on is how hard it is to contact him and the TA's. It takes a 1month+ to receive a grade on one essay. Overall the essays were pretty easy but instructions were often unclear as well as criteria for peerceptiv.

The class wasn't graded by the professor, and with 500 students it was unreasonable. There were 5 TAs but they weren't very helpful. Each unit required a 500–700 word essay and an image/chart every other week. We graded peers and had to schedule 30-min Zoom calls with 5 students, which was difficult. AI use was allowed but I wouldn't take it again.

Class is easy, and the essays are doable and only occur every two weeks. Discussions are hard to schedule but easy grades. Most quiz questions come from the textbook, but the essays matter more so no need to read as much. Make sure to keep track of Peerceptiv review and feedback deadlines. Professor is also difficult to reach via email.

Teacher updated syllabus to include a group project Lied to student that it was in the syllabus the whole time Student called her out and proved she updated it on nov 21 and she never responded but responded to other questions TAs take months to grade shortessay, awful at grading too, and grades depend on how accurately you can grade other's essays

The professor ( + TAs) are VERY slow & incompetent in the realm of grading. They use Peerceptiv, where your grade is partially based off your ability to MATCH another person's review of a peer's work, among other nonsense grading criteria. If your rating doesn't match up with the Peerceptiv algorithm (which is inaccessible) and others, points off.
You get rated on how well you grade other people makes no sense

Overall, an easy science class, but beware. Tophat virtual field trips were not graded easily, so make sure to do it properly and check with the material. There are group assignments, so try to have a few friends in the class. Tests are easy, and you get two tries. Not super reachable, however. Light class overall.
This class was awesome for a physical life and sciences credit. Typically took a couple hours a week to complete the work and the exams are open note and not difficult. Take this class!!

Attendance checks with short quiz every class. Lectures are terribly boring and over statistical methods, but the homework is in Rstudio. It feels like 2 entirely different classes. Midterm and final werent too bad and there is a group project. Overall, easy class but boring and unorganized.

Dr. Shobha Yadav was assigned this course because the previous professor couldn't teach it. The class was taught like a statistics and coding class. There are attendance checks every lecture and assignments every week as well as a group project. That being said, the class is not difficult and doesn't require ample time to do well.

Fairly easy online science credit. Class won't take up a lot of time if you keep up which isn't too hard. Doesn't use canvas except for projects, she uses tophat for modules. Modules can have about 40-50 assignments each and she gives you about 3 to 4 weeks to complete. Tests are easy and she's very understanding about late work.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework
